rows.parameterName: Identification (residue turns pink again with sodium fluoride)
rows.expectedResultText: The residue, in contact with the crystals, turns pink again in a short time

tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.bpSpecification: Almost white, coarse powder, granules or flakes.

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble.

details.reference: BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.procedure: Identification test 1: in a platinum crucible mix 1.0 g sample with 5.0 g anhydrous lithium metaborate; heat slowly, ignite at 1000-1200 °C for 15 min; cool and crush. Take 0.25 g residue, mix with about 10 mg sodium fluoride and a few drops of sulfuric acid to a thin slurry; cover with a plastic plate with a drop of water suspended under it and warm gently. A white ring forms rapidly around the drop.

Identification test 2: dissolve 1.0 g of the residue (test 1) in 5 mL dilute hydrochloric acid and 10 mL water; filter; add ammonium chloride buffer pH 10.0 (white gelatinous precipitate); centrifuge and keep the supernatant for test 3. Dissolve the precipitate in dilute hydrochloric acid, add dilute sodium hydroxide dropwise (white gelatinous precipitate); filter, add phenolphthalein to the residue (pink), wash with water until colourless and still white with phenolphthalein; sprinkle sodium fluoride crystals on the residue: it turns pink again in a short time.

Identification test 3: to 2 mL of the supernatant from test 2 add 1 mL dilute ammonia R1 and 1 mL ammonium chloride solution (a white precipitate may form and dissolve on adding the ammonium chloride solution); add 1 mL disodium hydrogen phosphate solution. A white precipitate is formed.
Identification test 4 (AAS): the sample complies with the limits of the assay described in section 6.10 (assay for aluminium and magnesium).
Disperse 5.0 g in 100 mL carbon dioxide-free water; measure pH with a calibrated pH meter.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix V L. Determination of pH Values

tests.procedure: Viscosity (BP Method III, rotating viscometer): weigh a quantity equivalent to 25.0 g dried substance and transfer to a 1 L blender jar containing water at 25 ± 2 °C to make 500 g; blend exactly 3 min at 14 000-15 000 r/min; transfer to a 600 mL beaker and stand 5 min; sample temperature 33 ± 3 °C; read with calibrated viscometer, spindle No. 3, 60 r/min for exactly 6 min; if the reading is above 90% of full scale, repeat with spindle No. 4 (0.32 cm diameter, 4.05 cm immersion depth).

details.spindle: No. 3 at 60 r/min for 6 min; No. 4 if above 90% full scale
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix V H, Method III

tests.procedure: Arsenic limit test, main method (BP Appendix VII Method A): sample 16.6 g in 100 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, boil 15 min, decant through filter into 250 mL flask with repeated hot dilute hydrochloric acid extractions; dilute to 250.0 mL; take 5.0 mL to 25.0 mL; add 15 mL hydrochloric acid, 0.1 mL stannous chloride solution and 5 mL potassium iodide solution, stand 15 min; add 5 g activated zinc and connect the gas evolution apparatus into silver diethyldithiocarbamate solution (3.0 mL) with lead acetate cotton. Compare colour after at least 2 h with the standard (1 mL of 1 ppm arsenic solution diluted to 25 mL). The sample colour must not be more intense than the standard (NMT 3 ppm). The alternative AAS method is not transcribed.

details.acid: 100 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, boil 15 min
details.standard: 1 mL of 1 ppm arsenic solution diluted to 25 mL
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix VII Limit Tests, Method A

tests.procedure: Lead limit test by AAS: test solution 10.0 g in 100 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, boil 15 min, decant and extract insoluble matter with hot water, concentrate filtrates to about 20 mL, dilute to 50.0 mL with water. Reference solutions from lead standard solution (10 ppm Pb). Lead hollow-cathode lamp, 217 nm, air-acetylene flame, calibrated AAS, single-point standardisation. NMT 15 ppm.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II D, Atomic Spectrophotometry: Absorption

tests.procedure: Loss on drying (BP Appendix IX D): weigh an empty crucible previously dried at 110 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh 1.000 g sample (W1); dry in calibrated oven at 110 °C for 2 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

Acid demand: weigh sample equivalent to 5.00 g dried substance; disperse in 500 mL water with constant mixing in a blender jar. Add 3.0 mL portions of 0.1 M hydrochloric acid at 5 s, 65 s, 125 s, 185 s, 245 s, 305 s, 365 s, 425 s, 485 s, 545 s, 605 s, 665 s and 725 s, and a 1.0 mL portion at 785 s. Determine pH at 840 s; the pH must not be greater than 4.0.

Assay by AAS (Al / Mg ratio). Aluminium: fuse 0.200 g sample with 1.0 g anhydrous lithium metaborate in platinum crucible at 1000-1200 °C for 15 min; dissolve in 75 mL of 50 g/L nitric acid; make to 200.0 mL (solution A). Take 20.0 mL of A, add 20 mL sodium chloride solution 10 g/L, dilute to 100.0 mL. Standards: 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 mL of aluminium 1 mg/mL solution in 0.20 g sodium chloride each made to 100.0 mL; blank 0.20 g sodium chloride in 100.0 mL. Aluminium hollow-cathode lamp, 309 nm, acetylene-nitrous oxide flame. Magnesium: take 25.0 mL of A to 50.0 mL; take 5.0 mL, add 20.0 mL lanthanum chloride solution, dilute to 100.0 mL. Standards: 5.0, 10.0, 15.0 and 20.0 mL of magnesium solution (diluted 5.0 mL to 500.0 mL), each with 20.0 mL lanthanum chloride, made to 100.0 mL; blank 20 mL lanthanum chloride to 100.0 mL. Magnesium hollow-cathode lamp, 285 nm, air-acetylene flame. Ratio Al/Mg must be 0.5 to 1.2.

details.solventA: 50 g/L nitric acid, 75 mL then to 200.0 mL

aluminium.naClSolution: 20 mL sodium chloride 10 g/L, to 100.0 mL
aluminium.standards: 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 mL of 1 mg/mL Al, each with 0.20 g NaCl, to 100.0 mL

magnesium.standards: 5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0 mL of Mg solution (5.0 mL of 1 mg/mL to 500.0 mL), each with 20.0 mL lanthanum chloride, to 100.0 mL
magnesium.blank: 20 mL lanthanum chloride solution to 100.0 mL

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II D, Atomic Spectrophotometry: Emission and Absorption, Method I

tests.procedure: Microbial enumeration (USP 2024 <2021>): 10 g sample in SCDB with 4% polysorbate 20 to 100 mL; within 1 h pipette 1 mL of the dilution into each of four plates; add SCDA to two plates and SDA to two plates; incubate SCDA 3-5 days at 30-35 °C (TAMC) and SDA 5-7 days at 20-25 °C (TYMC); count, average the plates and express as CFU/gm x DF (DF = 10).
Yeasts and molds: as TAMC, SDA plates incubated 5-7 days at 20-25 °C; express as CFU/gm x DF (DF = 10).

Specified microorganism E. coli: incubate SCDB'' 18-24 h at 30-35 °C; transfer 1 mL to 100 mL MacConkey broth (MBP), 42-44 °C 24-48 h; subculture on MacConkey agar (MAR) 30-35 °C 18-72 h; confirm by Gram stain, EMB (30-35 °C 24-48 h) and TBX (42-44 °C 18-72 h); optionally confirm identity with an identification system (probability above 70%).

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph of Aluminium Magnesium Silicate
